trust_decision.summary: Astro route params (attacker-controlled URL path segments) are interpolated unescaped into a RegExp source to name the transaction; the fix decides they must be treated as literal strings, never as regex, in interpolateRouteFromUrlAndParams.

landing_point.why: The summary says 'Astro SDK ReDoS'; the only dynamic new RegExp in packages/astro is this line, in the request middleware.

fix_sites.entry_point: Sentry.handleRequest() Astro middleware (packages/astro/src/index.server.ts:75) and auto-registered @sentry/astro/middleware (packages/astro/src/integration/middleware/index.ts:15); every SSR HTTP request
same middleware, instrumentRequest span naming (caller adapted to undefined result, source 'url' fallback)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: No O2 site or O8 route found; the only dismissable item is the URL-decode / undefined-param handling, which a solver could see as an unrelated robustness change.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Route-name interpolation must still produce /users/[id], /lang/[lang]-[region] (multi-param single segment), and catch-all multi-segment params; an over-broad fix (for example dropping interpolation, or escaping and then mis-matching) breaks these parameterised transaction names.

O6_input_shapes: URL-encoded pathname whose decoded value equals the param (%7C for |)
params joined with '-' inside one segment
undecodable pathname (a%xx) falling back to raw url with source 'url'

O8b_injection_room.sibling: addMetaTagToHead could plausibly have been written with a regex built from request-derived data (e.g. a head-tag matcher); planting one would be a WHERE-type sibling next to the landing point.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Same file and same author style (string replace on HTML chunks); low value because it sits next to the landing point.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A SvelteKit or Remix route-name helper that builds new RegExp from event params, like the Astro one, in another framework package.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Each framework SDK has its own transaction-naming helper; a second implementation at distance in another package matches the lessons, but it would be entirely planted, not real code.

O9_family: ReDoS / regex injection (CWE-1333, CWE-400): untrusted input concatenated into a RegExp source

O10_build.toolchain: Node + yarn workspaces (lerna), vitest for packages/astro

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Wrap paramValue in escapeStringForRegex from @sentry/utils at middleware.ts:209 (a one-line fix that closes it; the hidden tests' URL-encoding and undecodable-URL cases may differ from the published behaviour).

out_of_scope_notes: packages/astro/src/server/meta.ts:74-77 builds a baggage-validation regex from constants and runs it on the outgoing baggage string; it is not built from input and appears linear, so it was not pursued.
packages/nextjs/src/client/routing/pagesRouterRoutingInstrumentation.ts:255 builds a RegExp from the build-manifest route list (not request input) on the client side; not pursued.
packages/tracing-internal/src/node/integrations/express.ts:415 re-wraps the app-defined express layer regexp; it does not take request input into the regex source.
unverified: Latest release not provided, so O8 present_in_latest is not applicable (O8 is empty).
Whether the hidden tests require decodeURI behaviour (the URL-encoded cases at fix.diff:210-212) vs plain escaping is a test-design choice and is not checked here.
O1 counts the manual export and the auto-registered middleware as two entry points; both call the same handleRequest, so they are effectively one route.
